evidence.quote: Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) Large Language Models (LLMs) fundamentally rely on high-quality training data.
The refined dataset immediately feeds back into model training, creating a dynamic feedback loop where improved model capabilities inform subsequent optimization cycles.
evidence.support_explanation: The loop is dataset refinement -> weight fine-tuning -> diagnostics from the updated weights.

evidence.quote: the base model is fine-tuned for one epoch on the dataset optimized in that specific iteration
evidence.support_explanation: Each iteration is a base-model SFT run; the evaluated artifact is the fine-tuned weights.

evidence.quote: We can see that Middo consistently enhances model performance across all benchmarks, achieving an average accuracy increase of
evidence.support_explanation: Claimed effect is benchmark accuracy of fine-tuned LLaMA-3.1-8B / Mistral-7B.

evidence.quote: Middo relies on the model being fine-tuned itself for identifying data quality and complexity.
evidence.support_explanation: Diagnostic signals come from the weights under training; no agent harness component (prompt/skill/tool/workflow/memory/evaluator) is retained or reused.

evidence.quote: In each iteration, after the three data selection and optimization processes described above, the optimized dataset is then fed back for the next round of model training.
evidence.support_explanation: The only consumer of the refined dataset is the next round of weight training.

evidence.quote: the base model is fine-tuned for one epoch on the dataset optimized in that specific iteration
evidence.support_explanation: Each iteration's product is a fine-tuned checkpoint.

evidence.quote: Models trained with Middo optimized data achieve consistent performance gains over baselines
evidence.support_explanation: The evaluated object is the trained model, not a reusable non-weight harness component.

rs_pattern.reason: Informational (out_of_scope): model-signal gates (loss thresholds, kNN sparsity, self-alignment scores) select samples, an LLM rewrites/extends them, and the model is retrained on the refined set each iteration — C08's generate→gate→retrain loop with 'per-instance loss threshold' and 'model self-scoring' gates and the training distribution as the manufactured object.

matches.tactic_steps_checked: C08: data defect named (static curation ignores model state) → LLM rewrite/neighbour-conditioned extension → threshold gates on model signals → retrain → iterate with the improved model re-diagnosing.
matches.success_checks: Iterated loop run on Alpaca/WizardLM with two base models (author-reported).
matches.failure_checks: Iteration count and thresholds are tuned on the reported benchmarks (App. 8.2–8.3); not used as Harness-RSI evidence.
matches.reason: heterogeneous_decomposition (sol) describes the three detectors but its load-bearing artifact is an error/fidelity decomposition for differentiated compression (sol itself rejected C04); the executed loop is C08, consistent with r06a SyncLoop.

assessment.claim_support_note: Not assessed under this rubric; Table 1–3 gains are author-reported SFT results.

G.reason: out_of_scope (rubric A3; EVIDENCE.md excludes weight-updating self-improvement). Boundary checked independently: Middo's retained, iteratively rewritten artifact is the SFT dataset, but that dataset is never read at inference — each iteration it is consumed only by re-fine-tuning the base model for one epoch (opus:O01, opus:O02), and every reported result (Tables 1–3, 5–7) is a fine-tuned LLaMA-3.1-8B/Mistral-7B checkpoint (opus:O03). The loss/embedding/self-alignment diagnostics are a training-data curriculum, not a prompt/skill/tool/workflow/memory/evaluator/config retained and reused by a frozen system; same ruling as r06a SyncLoop (evolved training data + retraining). Not scored; null is not a zero-quality rating.
